Activity: Read Rails Guides on routing end-to-end. Trace a request from router to controller to view in a sample app.
Read ActionDispatch middleware stack source. Run `rake middleware` and understand each layer.
Read Rails Guides on Active Record fully. Focus on connection handling and query interface.
Study Arel and how AR builds SQL. Run `to_sql` on complex queries. Practice joins vs includes vs eager_load vs preload.
Study AR callbacks lifecycle. Map out the full callback chain for create/update/destroy.
Generate BillFlow app (no scaffold). Create Client model with: name, email, company, phone, notes. Write migration with indexes.
Create Project model: belongs_to Client, has name, description, hourly_rate, status (enum: active/archived/completed). Add foreign key constraints.
Create TimeEntry model: belongs_to Project, has description, started_at, ended_at, billable (boolean). Add validation for ended_at > started_at.
Study strong_migrations gem. Understand why certain migrations are dangerous. Write complex migrations with conditional indexes.

Create Invoice model: belongs_to Client, has number (auto-generated), status (draft/sent/paid/overdue), issued_on, due_on, notes. Create LineItem model: belongs_to Invoice, has description, quantity, unit_price.
Add model validations and associations throughout. Implement Invoice#total, Invoice#generate_number, and TimeEntry#duration methods. Write scopes: Invoice.overdue, Project.active, TimeEntry.billable.
Read controller source. Understand filters/params/rendering/redirecting internals.
Build ClientsController with full CRUD. No scaffolding. Strong params with nested attributes. Before actions for shared lookups.
Build ProjectsController nested under clients. Build TimeEntriesController nested under projects. Handle the nested routing properly.
Study partials/layouts/helpers. Understand the rendering pipeline. Build custom form builders.
Build application layout with navigation. Create Client views: index (with project counts), show (with projects list), form partial with validations displayed.
Build Project views with time entry log. Build TimeEntry form that calculates duration. Create Invoice views: index with status badges, show with line items table and totals.
Study Propshaft vs Sprockets. Configure import maps or CSS bundling. Set up Tailwind CSS for the project.
Style BillFlow with Tailwind: professional layout, responsive sidebar nav, status badges, data tables. Make it look like a real product.
Set up Active Storage. Understand direct uploads and variants.
Add file attachments to Projects (contracts, briefs). Display attached files on project show page. Add avatar uploads to Clients.
Build transactional email system. Set up previews and test delivery.
Build InvoiceMailer: sends invoice to client with PDF attachment (plain HTML for now). Build ReminderMailer: sends overdue notice. Create mailer previews for both.
Build invoice creation workflow: select a client, choose unbilled time entries, auto-generate line items from time entries, review and save as draft.
Review and polish. Add seed file with realistic sample data (5 clients, 10 projects, 50 time entries, 8 invoices in various states). Verify all CRUD flows work end-to-end.
Read Rails testing guide fully. Understand test types and when to use each.
Write model tests for Client, Project, TimeEntry: validations, associations, scopes, and custom methods (duration, total, generate_number).
Write model tests for Invoice and LineItem. Test the invoice creation workflow: generating from time entries, status transitions, total calculations.
Set up factory_bot. Create factories for all models with traits (e.g. invoice :paid :overdue). Compare to fixtures approach.
Write controller tests for ClientsController and ProjectsController. Test CRUD operations and authorization edge cases.
Write controller tests for InvoicesController including the multi-step creation flow. Test TimeEntriesController.
Study integration and system tests. Set up Capybara for system tests.
Write system tests for critical flows: create client → create project → log time → generate invoice → send invoice. Test the full happy path.
Learn mocks/stubs/spies. Study when to use real objects vs doubles. Practice testing service objects.
Write mailer tests for InvoiceMailer and ReminderMailer. Test email content and recipients. Mock external delivery.
Master debug gem. Set up SimpleCov and RuboCop. Identify untested paths.
Run SimpleCov, identify gaps, write tests to reach 90%+ on models. Fix RuboCop offenses in the project.
Study SOLID principles applied to Rails. Practice extract method/extract class patterns.
Refactor BillFlow: extract InvoiceGenerator service object from controller. Extract TimeEntry.billable_for_client scope. Clean up any fat controller actions.
Full test suite review. Ensure all edge cases covered: what happens when invoice has zero line items? When time entry has no end time? Run full suite green.
Read Hotwire docs on Turbo Drive. Understand how it intercepts links and forms. Practice disabling selectively.
Enable Turbo Drive in BillFlow. Fix any forms that break. Add data-turbo-method where needed. Ensure flash messages work with Turbo.
Study Turbo Frames: lazy loading and scoped navigation. Build practice examples with inline editing.
Add inline editing to time entries: click a row to edit in-place without page reload. Use Turbo Frames to scope the edit form to just that row.
Add tabbed interface on Project show page: Overview / Time Entries / Files / Invoices. Each tab loads via Turbo Frame (lazy loaded).
Study Turbo Streams: append/prepend/replace/remove. Understand broadcast from models via Action Cable.
Add Turbo Stream responses to TimeEntry create/update/destroy: entries appear/update/remove from the list without page reload.
Add real-time invoice status updates: when an invoice is marked as paid, all connected clients see the status change live via broadcast.
Read Stimulus handbook. Understand controllers/targets/values/actions lifecycle.
Build a live time tracking timer with Stimulus: start/stop button, running clock display, auto-saves when stopped. Store timer state in Stimulus values.
Build invoice line item editor with Stimulus: dynamically add/remove line items, auto-calculate row totals and invoice grand total as user types quantities/prices.
Build debounced client search: type in search box, Stimulus controller fires request after 300ms pause, results load in Turbo Frame.
Study Stimulus lifecycle callbacks and reusable controller patterns. Explore stimulus-use library.
Add dropdown menus, confirmation modals for delete actions, and toast notifications using Stimulus controllers. No external JS libraries.
Install ViewComponent gem. Understand slots/previews/testing patterns.
Extract reusable components: StatusBadge (draft/sent/paid/overdue), DataTable (sortable headers), EmptyState, StatCard (for dashboard metrics).
Build BillFlow dashboard with ViewComponents and Turbo Frames: total revenue, outstanding invoices, hours this week, recent activity. Each card is a lazy-loaded frame.
Add mini charts to dashboard (revenue over time, hours by project). Use a simple charting approach (CSS-only bar charts or Chart.js with Stimulus controller).
Build in-app notification system: flash messages via Turbo Streams, notification dropdown with unread count, mark as read. Broadcast new notifications in real-time.
Polish all Hotwire interactions. Ensure no full page reloads for common actions. Add loading states (Turbo frame loading indicators). Test all Stimulus controllers.
Read Active Job guide. Understand adapters and queues. Write a basic job.
Set up Solid Queue. Configure multiple queues with priorities. Understand the database-backed approach.
Create InvoiceGeneratorJob: generates PDF invoice using Prawn or wicked_pdf. Attach PDF to invoice record via Active Storage. Update invoice status when complete.
Move invoice sending to background: SendInvoiceJob generates PDF then emails it. Add job status tracking so user sees 'Sending...' state on the UI via Turbo Stream.
Study idempotent jobs and retry strategies. Implement failure handling with dead letter patterns.
Build BulkInvoiceJob: generate invoices for all clients with unbilled time in one click. Process each client as a sub-job. Report progress via Turbo Streams.
Build ExportJob: export time entries or invoices to CSV for a date range. Large exports run in background. Notify user via Turbo Stream when file is ready for download.
Deep dive into Action Cable. Understand channels/subscriptions/broadcasting.
Use Action Cable to sync the running timer across browser tabs. If timer is running in one tab, show the active timer in other tabs. Handle connection/disconnection.
Set up recurring jobs with Solid Queue. Understand cron-style scheduling.
Create recurring jobs: OverdueInvoiceCheckerJob (daily, marks invoices overdue and sends reminder), WeeklyReportJob (sends weekly hours summary email to freelancer).
Test all jobs thoroughly. Handle edge cases: what if PDF generation fails? What if email bounces? Add retry limits and error notifications to the freelancer.
Study REST API design. Understand versioning strategies and JSON response patterns.
Create API::V1 namespace. Build API::V1::ClientsController and API::V1::TimeEntriesController with JSON responses. Use jbuilder views for serialization.
Study API authentication approaches: API keys vs JWT vs OAuth2.
Implement API token auth for BillFlow: generate API keys in user settings, authenticate via Authorization header, scope all queries to token owner.
Build remaining API endpoints: Projects (CRUD), Invoices (read-only), Timer (start/stop). Return proper status codes and error responses.
Study Rack::Attack. Configure throttles per endpoint and per API key.
Add rate limiting to BillFlow API: 100 requests/minute per key. Return 429 with Retry-After header. Add rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining) to all responses.
Study webhook patterns: signatures and async processing and retry strategies.
Build outgoing webhooks: allow users to register a URL. Fire webhooks on invoice.paid, timer.stopped, invoice.overdue events. Queue delivery via background job with exponential backoff.
Read Stripe docs on Checkout/Products/Prices. Understand the payment flow and webhook events.
Integrate Stripe: create a 'Pay Invoice' flow where clients click a link in their invoice email, land on a payment page, and pay via Stripe Checkout. Handle checkout.session.completed webhook.
Handle Stripe webhook events: mark invoice as paid when payment succeeds. Handle payment_failed. Store Stripe charge ID on invoice for reference. Verify webhook signatures.
Build a simple client portal: clients access via a signed token URL (no login needed). They see their invoices and can pay outstanding ones. Read-only view of project progress.
Study Faraday for HTTP clients. Implement timeout/retry/circuit breaker patterns.
Integrate a free currency exchange API: if invoice currency differs from client currency, fetch and display converted total. Cache rates for 24h. Handle API downtime gracefully.
Write API documentation (in-app or simple markdown). Test all API endpoints with integration tests. Verify Stripe webhook handling end-to-end in test mode.
Install bullet gem. Study EXPLAIN ANALYZE output. Learn to read query plans.
Run bullet on all BillFlow pages. Fix every N+1 detected: client index (projects count), invoice index (line items total), dashboard (multiple aggregations). Verify with query logs.
Study index strategies: composite/partial/covering indexes. Read Use The Index Luke.
Add strategic indexes to BillFlow: composite index on time_entries(project_id, billable, started_at), partial index on invoices WHERE status != 'paid'. Benchmark before/after.
Study Russian Doll caching. Understand cache keys and touch cascading.
Add fragment caching to BillFlow: cache client cards on index, cache project sidebar, cache invoice line items table. Use touch to invalidate parent caches.
Study Rails.cache store options. Understand TTL and eviction strategies.
Cache expensive dashboard calculations: monthly revenue, total outstanding, hours this week. Invalidate on relevant model changes. Add counter caches for project time_entries_count.
Study rack-mini-profiler and memory profiling. Understand object allocation.
Profile BillFlow with rack-mini-profiler. Identify slowest pages. Optimize: batch find_each for reports, reduce memory in PDF generation, optimize Active Storage variant processing.
Study load testing with k6 or similar. Understand concurrency bottlenecks.
Load test BillFlow: hit dashboard, client index, and invoice creation under 50 concurrent users. Identify bottlenecks. Add database connection pooling config. Re-test and document improvements.
Optimize BillFlow frontend: lazy load below-fold Turbo Frames, compress images, add preload hints for critical assets. Measure Core Web Vitals before/after.
Final performance pass: ensure all pages load under 200ms locally. Document all optimizations made and their impact. Run full test suite to verify nothing broke.
Write a Dockerfile for Rails. Understand layers and multi-stage builds.
Write production Dockerfile for BillFlow: multi-stage build, asset precompilation, proper user permissions. Create docker-compose.yml for local dev: app + postgres + solid_queue worker.
Read Kamal docs. Understand how it deploys containers to bare servers.
Configure Kamal for BillFlow: set up deploy.yml with accessories (PostgreSQL, Solid Queue worker). Configure health checks and environment variables via .env.
Provision a VPS (Hetzner/DigitalOcean/etc). Deploy BillFlow with Kamal. Run migrations, seed data, verify the app works in production.
Study rolling deployments and health checks. Understand blue-green vs rolling strategies.
Practice zero-downtime deploy: add a migration, deploy, verify no dropped requests. Configure Kamal boot timeout and health check path.
Study production database management: backups/restores/migrations under load.
Set up automated daily PostgreSQL backups with pg_dump to object storage. Write a restore script and test it. Practice point-in-time recovery.
Study application monitoring and structured logging approaches.
Add Lograge for structured JSON logs. Set up error tracking (Sentry or Honeybadger). Add custom instrumentation with ActiveSupport::Notifications for invoice generation timing.
Configure alerts: error rate spikes, job queue depth, response time thresholds. Set up uptime monitoring for BillFlow's production URL.
Study OWASP Top 10 and Rails security best practices. Learn Brakeman.
Run Brakeman on BillFlow. Fix all warnings. Implement CSP headers. Audit: are API tokens hashed? Are Stripe keys in ENV? Is CSRF protection solid? Add brute-force protection to client portal.
Study GitHub Actions for Rails apps. Understand test/lint/security scan pipelines.
Set up GitHub Actions for BillFlow: run tests, RuboCop, Brakeman on every push. Auto-deploy to production on merge to main via Kamal.
Configure custom domain with SSL for BillFlow. Set up proper DNS. Configure ActionMailer host settings for production email links.
Full production readiness check: backups verified, monitoring live, CI green, SSL working, error tracking capturing, logs structured. Run through every feature in production.
Study service object patterns. Command pattern with result objects.

Extract services from BillFlow: InvoiceGenerator (creates invoice from time entries), InvoiceSender (generates PDF + emails), PaymentProcessor (handles Stripe flow). Each returns a Result object with success/failure.
Study form objects for complex multi-model forms.
Build TimerForm: handles creating a time entry with optional new project creation in one form. Build InvoiceForm: validates line items, calculates totals, handles nested attributes cleanly.
Study query object pattern. Make queries composable and testable.
Extract query objects: ClientRevenueQuery (total revenue per client with date range), UnbilledTimeQuery (time entries ready for invoicing), OverdueInvoicesQuery (with days overdue calculation).
Study Pundit for authorization. Build policy objects.

Add Pundit to BillFlow: InvoicePolicy (can only send if draft, can only mark paid if sent), ProjectPolicy (can only archive if no unbilled time), TimeEntryPolicy (can only edit if invoice is still draft).
Study presenter/decorator pattern with Draper or plain Ruby.

Create decorators: InvoiceDecorator (formatted total, status label, due date display), ClientDecorator (full address, outstanding balance display), TimeEntryDecorator (formatted duration, date range).
Study AASM gem. Model complex workflows as state machines.
Implement Invoice state machine: draft → sent → viewed → paid (or overdue). Add guards (can't send without line items), callbacks (email on send, webhook on paid), and event logging.
Study pub/sub with ActiveSupport::Notifications or Wisper. Understand decoupling benefits.

Implement domain events in BillFlow: InvoicePaid fires webhook + updates dashboard cache + sends receipt. TimerStopped creates time entry + updates project stats. Decouple side effects from core logic.
Study multi-tenant approaches. Understand row-based vs schema-based.
Add multi-tenancy to BillFlow: multiple freelancer accounts on one instance. Row-based with ActsAsTenant or current_account pattern. Each freelancer sees only their own data. Add account switcher UI.
Study Rails Engines. Understand mountable vs full engines.
Extract BillFlow's client portal into a mountable engine: separate routes, controllers, views. The portal can be mounted at /portal and has its own layout.
Study Ruby metaprogramming: define_method/method_missing/class_eval. How Rails uses these patterns internally.
Build a small DSL for BillFlow: a reportable concern that lets models declare `reportable :field_name` to auto-generate aggregation methods and scopes. Test it on TimeEntry and Invoice.
Review all patterns applied. Write tests for every service/form/query/policy object. Ensure the refactored code is cleaner than before. Run full suite green.
Add proper user authentication (Devise or custom). Registration, login, password reset, session management. Lock down all controllers to require authentication.
Build onboarding flow: after signup, guide user through creating first client, first project, and logging first time entry. Track onboarding completion.
Build user settings page: profile info, timezone, default currency, invoice template preferences, Stripe API key configuration, webhook URL management.
Build reporting section: revenue by month chart, hours by project breakdown, client profitability analysis, year-over-year comparison. Use cached query objects.
Build downloadable reports: monthly income summary PDF and annual tax export CSV. Generate in background and notify when ready.
Custom error pages (404/500) matching BillFlow's design. Add global exception handling for API. Friendly error messages for validation failures throughout.
Add meta tags, OpenGraph tags for client portal public pages, sitemap for marketing pages. Configure proper canonical URLs.
Accessibility audit: keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, color contrast, focus states. Fix all issues found. Test with browser accessibility tools.
Responsive testing: every page works on phone/tablet. Fix layout issues. Make timer especially mobile-friendly (big start/stop button).
Build a marketing landing page for BillFlow: feature highlights, pricing, signup CTA. Serves as the root path for logged-out users.
Write system tests for the 5 most critical flows. Run full test suite. Fix any flaky tests. Verify 85%+ coverage.
Final production checklist: ENV vars set, seeds removed, debug code removed, Stripe in live mode, DNS propagated, SSL valid, backups running, monitoring active.
Deploy final version. Sign up as a real user. Create a real client and invoice. Send a real invoice and receive a real payment. BillFlow is live.
Invite 3-5 freelancer friends to use BillFlow. Monitor error tracking and logs closely. Note UX friction points they report.
Fix the top 3 bugs or UX issues reported by beta users. Deploy fixes with zero downtime.
Add one feature beta users requested that you didn't plan. Practice the full cycle: plan, build, test, deploy.
Write a retrospective: what worked, what was harder than expected, what you'd do differently. List every Rails concept you used in this project.
Read Devise source. Understand how Warden middleware and strategies work under the hood.
Read Turbo Rails source. Understand how broadcasts and stream helpers are implemented.
Read Solid Queue source. Trace how a job goes from enqueue to execution.
Read a Discourse feature end-to-end: pick one feature and read model/controller/view/jobs/tests.
Read Pay gem source (or Stripe integration in a real app). Compare their approach to what you built in BillFlow.
Find a Rails issue labeled 'good first issue'. Read the contributing guide. Understand the PR process.
Submit a documentation fix or small bug fix to Rails or a gem you used in BillFlow.
Review 2-3 open PRs on gems you used (Solid Queue / ViewComponent / AASM). Leave helpful review comments.
Extract one reusable piece of BillFlow into a standalone gem or open-source repo: maybe your invoice PDF generator, timer Stimulus controller, or webhook delivery system.
Write a blog post about the most interesting technical challenge you solved in BillFlow. Explain the problem and your solution.
Answer 3 Rails questions on Stack Overflow. Research deeply and provide thorough answers with code examples.

Review your journey. Compare your Day 1 code to your Day 170 code. List 10 things you can do now that you couldn't before. Plan what's next: another app, consulting, teaching, contributing to Rails core.
